newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia state bank to float one billion shares.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia state bank to float one billion shares.

text.p: Indonesia announced its next major privatisation plan on Monday, saying it will divest up to a 25 percent-stake in giant state-owned bank PT Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) later this year.

"We expect to list up to a 25 percent stake, or one billion shares, on the Jakarta and Surabaya stock exchanges in November and plan to use the proceeds for short and long-term credit growth," BNI president director Widigdo Sukarman told reporters.
The listing of BNI, Indonesia's largest state-owned bank with total assets of around 32.4 trillion rupiah ($14.09 billion) as of June 30, 1996, is the fifth major listing of state firms since 1991.
Sukarman said he was confident that the response from both local and foreign investors would be positive despite the relatively huge amount of shares to be offered.
"The bank is embarking on a busy roadshow to six large business cities in Indonesia and various financial centres in Asia, Europe and the U.S. and Canada to attract investors," he said.
Sukarman said the domestic roadshow started on Monday and will last till October 3, while the overseas tour was scheduled between October 14 to October 24.
A final decision on the pricing was expected to be announced on October 24 followed by the public offer between November 6 and November 11 and listing on November 29, Sukarman said.
Sukarman declined to reveal the expected price range of the shares and the expected amount of the proceeds, but said the nominal value would be 500 rupiah per share.
Analysts said proceeds were likely to range between 900 billion rupiah to one trillion rupiah.
Sukarman said the funds would be used to boost the bank's short- and long-term credit growth.
BNI extended 20.44 trillion rupiah credit in the first six months of 1996 against 17.32 trillion rupiah in the same period last year, he said.
Sukarman did not give figures for either long-term or short-term credit, but said most of the funds went to the manufacturing sector followed by agriculture, trade and tourism.
"We expect to have a credit growth of around 17 percent and a net profit of between 320 to 330 billion rupiah this year," he said.
BNI posted a net profit of 146.2 billion rupiah in the first six months of 1996 against 131.3 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
It posted a net profit of 274 billion rupiah in 1995 against 151.9 billion rupiah in 1994.
Wahzary Wardaya, director of lead underwriter Danareksa Sekuritas, told reporters that there was unlikely to be a discount for investors.
"The pricing policy will be based on the assumption that it will benefit both retail and institutional investors and that it should reflect market demand," Wardaya said.

Indonesia has listed four state-owned firms since 1991, including telecommunications giants PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia, PT Indonesia Satellite Corporation, the world's largest tin miner PT Tambang Timah and cement firm Semen Gresik.
